documents.title: H&P - Admission - COPD Exacerbation
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 04:20, HD1
CC: shortness of breath, wheezing x 3 days
HPI:
52 yo F with known COPD (GOLD C, FEV1 48% predicted 2 yrs ago) presents with 3 days of worsening dyspnea, productive cough with yellow sputum.
Started after URI symptoms in household. Using home albuterol MDI q2h with minimal relief.
Unable to complete sentences on arrival. Denies chest pain, fever, leg swelling, orthopnea.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Mild accessory muscle use noted at triage, resolved after first nebulizer; respiratory rate 22.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
BiPAP trialed for 40 minutes in the ED, removed for patient comfort; not resumed.
Magnesium 2 g IV given at 03:20. Azithromycin 500 mg IV started.
PMH:
COPD, 2 prior admissions for exacerbation, no prior intubation
HTN
GERD
Anxiety
Osteopenia
SOCIAL:
40 pack-year smoker, still smoking ~half PPD. No alcohol. No illicit drugs.
Lives with daughter in a 2nd floor apartment. Independent with ADLs, baseline dyspnea at one flight of stairs.
No home oxygen.
FAMILY HX: mother with COPD, father MI in 60s
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash
HOME MEDS:
tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
lisinopril 10 mg daily
pantoprazole 40 mg daily
sertraline 50 mg daily
ROS: positive for cough, sputum, wheeze, fatigue. Negative for fever, chills, hemoptysis, calf pain, rash.
EXAM:
Vitals 04:20: T 37.1, HR 104, BP 142/86, RR 22, SpO2 91% on 4L NC
Gen: fatigued, speaking in short phrases, sitting upright
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no JVD
Lungs: diffuse expiratory wheeze bilaterally, prolonged expiratory phase, poor air movement at bases
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur
Abd: soft, nontender, BS present
Ext: no edema, no calf tenderness
Neuro: alert and oriented x3, no asterixis
DATA:
WBC 13.2, Hgb 13.8, Plt 288
Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 101, CO2 29, BUN 14, Cr 0.8, glucose 128
Trop neg x1. BNP 48.
CXR: hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation or effusion
ECG: sinus tach 104, no acute ischemic changes
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
52 yo F with moderate-severe COPD presenting with acute exacerbation, likely viral/bacterial trigger, hypoxemic and wheezing despite ED therapy. Admit to stepdown.
1. COPD exacerbation - scheduled albuterol-ipratropium nebs q4h and q2h prn
IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
Continue azithromycin 500 mg IV daily, plan 5 day course
O2 to keep SpO2 88-92 percent via NC, wean as tolerated
RT to follow, hold further noninvasive ventilation unless clinical decline
2. HTN - hold lisinopril while volume status assessed, restart if BP stable
3. Hyperglycemia - steroid related, SSI q6h, check fingersticks q6h
4. Tobacco use - nicotine patch 14 mg offered, counseling in AM
5. DVT ppx: enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily
Discussed plan with pt and daughter at bedside. Full code.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:15
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports breathing somewhat improved overnight. Slept in recliner position. Still coughing yellow sputum.
No chest pain. Tolerated nebs. Did not require any noninvasive ventilation overnight.
OBJECTIVE:
Overnight fingersticks: 212 at 00:00, 342 at 06:00 - 8 units regular insulin given per sliding scale
Lungs: expiratory wheeze still present bilaterally, improved air movement compared to admission
No accessory muscle use this AM. Speaking in full sentences.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Ext no edema.
Labs: WBC 15.8 (steroid effect), K 3.8, Cr 0.8
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
COPD exacerbation, improving.
- Continue methylprednisolone 40 mg IV q8h
- Continue scheduled albuterol-ipratropium q4h, prn q2h
- Continue azithromycin, day 2 of 5
- Wean O2 to target SpO2 88-92 percent, attempt 2L NC today
- Steroid hyperglycemia: increase SSI to moderate scale, fingersticks q6h
- KCl 40 mEq PO x1 for K 3.8
- Mobilize with PT today, out of bed to chair
- Nicotine patch started, pt receptive to cessation discussion

documents.title: Progress Note - HD4
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD4 08:00
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt feels much better. Ambulated in hallway with RN yesterday evening without desaturation.
Cough now nonproductive. No dyspnea at rest. Reports mild tremor from nebs.
Appetite improved. No hypoglycemic symptoms.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.8, HR 84, BP 128/76, RR 18, SpO2 94% on room air
Ambulatory SpO2 91% on room air after 2 laps
Fingersticks past 24h: 188, 204, 176, 161
Lungs: mild scattered end-expiratory wheeze, good air movement throughout
No accessory muscle use. No pursed lip breathing at rest.
CV: RRR. Abd soft. Ext no edema.
Labs: WBC 11.1, K 4.2, Cr 0.7, glucose 166
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
COPD exacerbation, near baseline.
- Off supplemental O2 since 22:00 HD3, maintaining sats
- Transition to prednisone 40 mg PO daily, plan total 5 day course from transition
- Azithromycin day 4 of 5
- Resume home tiotropium and budesonide-formoterol today, RT to review inhaler technique
- Continue SSI, expect improvement as steroid tapers
- Restart lisinopril 10 mg daily, BP stable
- PT cleared, no equipment needs
- Anticipate discharge HD5 if stable overnight

documents.title: Discharge Summary - COPD Exacerbation
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted HD1, discharged HD5
Discharge diagnosis: acute exacerbation of COPD with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, resolved
Secondary: steroid induced hyperglycemia, HTN, tobacco use disorder, GERD
HOSPITAL COURSE:
52 yo F with moderate-severe COPD presented at 01:30 HD1 with 3 days of worsening dyspnea and wheeze following URI.
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Mild accessory muscle use noted at triage, resolved after first nebulizer; respiratory rate 22.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
BiPAP trialed for 40 minutes in the ED, removed for patient comfort; not resumed.
Admitted to stepdown. CXR showed hyperinflation without consolidation. Trop negative, BNP 48.
IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
Treated with scheduled albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers and azithromycin 500 mg daily x 5 days.
Oxygen weaned to room air by 22:00 HD3. Steroids transitioned to oral prednisone HD4.
Ambulatory saturation 91% on room air HD4. No further noninvasive ventilation required at any point after the ED.
Fingersticks normalized to 140s-160s by HD5 and insulin discontinued at discharge.
DISCHARGE EXAM HD5 09:10: T 36.7, HR 80, BP 126/74, RR 16, SpO2 94% RA. Lungs with minimal scattered wheeze, good air movement.
DISCHARGE MEDS:
prednisone 40 mg PO daily x 2 more days then stop
tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn wheeze
lisinopril 10 mg daily
pantoprazole 40 mg daily
sertraline 50 mg daily
nicotine patch 14 mg daily
FOLLOW UP:
Primary care in 5-7 days for symptom check and repeat glucose
Pulmonary clinic in 3-4 weeks, repeat spirometry when stable
Smoking cessation program referral placed, pt agreeable
INSTRUCTIONS:
Return for increasing shortness of breath, fever, chest pain, confusion, or need to use rescue inhaler more than q2h.
Inhaler technique reviewed with RT and teach-back completed with pt and daughter.
Discharged home ambulatory, stable on room air, at 11:40 HD5.
